simple.meaning: אֲכַל (ʼăkal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “accuse, devour, eat.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 3:8. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲכַל (H399) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֲכַל (ʼăkal) / H399 is traced through Daniel 3:8, Daniel 4:30, Daniel 6:25, Daniel 7:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: Therefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and brought accusation against the Jews.
The king spoke and said, “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
Then king Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages, who dwell in all the earth:
“Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’

“After this I saw in the night visions, and, behold, there was a fourth animal, awesome and powerful, and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet. It was different from all the animals that were before it. It had ten horns.

“Then I desired to know the truth concerning the fourth animal, which was different from all of them, exceedingly terrible, whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of bronze; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet;
“Thus he said, ‘The fourth animal will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms, and will devour the whole earth, and will tread it down, and break it in pieces.
